name: Cnidocyte Dermal Defense
description: Integrates cnidocyte cells from box jellyfish into the skin of the forearms, hands, and upper back, creating a contact-activated sting defense. When the skin is touched with sufficient pressure (a grab, a punch, a grapple), the cnidocytes fire microscopic barbed threads that deliver a potent neurotoxic sting. The pain is immediate, intense, and debilitating — comparable to a full-body jellyfish sting concentrated in the point of contact. The effect is purely defensive — it only activates on contact pressure, not casual touch. The user's own skin is immune. Crucible Genomics' installation includes a voluntary suppression system controlled through skin tension, allowing the user to shake hands without incident. Black-market versions often lack this refinement, making any firm contact dangerous.
procedure: Dermal injection matrix with cnidocyte cultivation, 3 sessions over 2 weeks
expression_time: 3–5 weeks; cnidocytes regenerate continuously after initial expression
reversibility: Reversible with targeted cell ablation; may require multiple treatments
side_effects: Skin in affected areas has a faintly translucent, gelatinous appearance
Cnidocytes occasionally fire during temperature extremes
Swimming in salt water causes mass cnidocyte discharge, creating a toxic cloud around the user
Suppression failure during sleep — bedpartners must be warned
social_perception: Feared and avoided. Stingerskin users are treated with physical distance. Handshakes are offered with visible tension. Intimate relationships require extraordinary trust. The modification is considered a last resort for people who face constant physical threat.
story_hooks: A stingerskin user is kidnapped — their captors are wearing gloves treated with a cnidocyte inhibitor that shouldn't exist outside Crucible Genomics' labs
A black-market stingerskin installation produces cnidocytes that fire chemical signals instead of toxin — someone is using unwitting recipients as biological sensor networks
